ready1_open_rewrite.rewritten_question_text: Venus and Earth revolve around the Sun in the same plane, and both revolution orbits are regarded as circular. As shown in the figure, when observed from Earth, the visual angle that Venus and the Sun can present (the Sun and Venus are both regarded as particles; the angle between the lines connecting them with the eye) has a maximum value. If the sine value of this maximum visual angle is n, then how is the revolution period of Venus expressed in terms of n?

ready2_open_rewrite.resolved_question_text: Venus and Earth revolve around the Sun in the same plane, and both revolution orbits are regarded as circular. As shown in the figure, when observed from Earth, the visual angle that Venus and the Sun can present (the Sun and Venus are both regarded as particles; the angle between the lines connecting them with the eye) has a maximum value. If the sine value of this maximum visual angle is n, then how is the revolution period of Venus expressed in terms of n?
ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows two approximately concentric circular orbits centered on the Sun. The inner circular orbit is labeled “Venus,” and the outer circular orbit is labeled “Earth.” The Sun is located near the center of the circle, indicating that Venus is an inner planet and Earth moves around the Sun in the outer orbit. Reasoning: Let the maximum visual angle be θ, the orbital radius of Venus be r_V, and the orbital radius of Earth be r_E. When the angle between Venus and the Sun as seen from Earth reaches its maximum, the line of sight from Earth to Venus is tangent to Venus’s circular orbit around the Sun, so the triangle “Sun-Venus-Earth” is right-angled at Venus. At this time θ is the angle at Earth formed by the direction toward the Sun and the direction toward Venus, so sin θ = opposite side/hypotenuse = r_V/r_E. The problem gives the sine value of the maximum visual angle as n, so r_V/r_E = n. By Kepler’s third law, T_V^2/T_E^2 = (r_V/r_E)^3 = n^3. If the Earth’s revolution period T_E=1 year is used as the unit, then T_V = √(n^3).
